title: Asterisk — Overview
description: Asterisk exporter dashboard: live status + history for calls, trunks, voice quality, ARI and Asterisk internals.

options.content:
## Asterisk monitoring
**Top row = right now. Every graph below = history** (use the time picker top-right; default last 6 h, refresh 30 s).
Pick one or more servers in **Server** above. Hover the **ⓘ** on any panel for what it means and what "bad" looks like.

| Term | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Channel** | one call leg. A normal call = 2 channels (caller side + callee side). Box load = channels. |
| **Call** | channels grouped into one conversation (Linkedid). Includes ARI-originated calls. |
| **Asterisk active calls** | Asterisk's own number (`core show calls`): only channels running dialplan, so ARI-originated legs are *not* counted. On ARI boxes it is much lower than *Call*. |
| **ASR** | answered ÷ attempted calls. Trend metric; CDR is the billing-grade source. |

panels.title: Asterisk
panels.description: Exporter can talk to Asterisk over AMI. DOWN = Asterisk stopped, AMI disabled, or wrong AMI credentials. While DOWN, other panels show the last known values.

panels.title: AMI connection
panels.description: Live AMI socket. Flaps here with Asterisk UP usually mean network or manager.conf issues.

panels.title: ARI
panels.description: ARI HTTP answered with valid credentials. N/A = ARI collector not configured on this server (normal for non-ARI boxes).

panels.title: Version
panels.description: Asterisk version reported over AMI.

panels.title: Uptime
panels.description: Time since Asterisk started. A sudden drop to minutes = Asterisk restarted.

panels.title: Since last reload
panels.description: Time since the last 'core reload' / module reload.

panels.title: Calls now
panels.description: Active calls (one per conversation, includes ARI-originated). Sparkline = recent trend.

panels.title: Channels now
panels.description: Active channels = call legs = real load on the box (CPU, RTP ports, licences).

panels.title: Asterisk active calls
panels.description: Asterisk's own count from 'core show calls' (dialplan channels only). Lower than 'Calls now' on ARI boxes — that is expected.

panels.title: Call attempts / min
panels.description: New calls per minute (5 min average).

panels.title: ASR (15 min)
panels.description: Answered ÷ attempted calls over the last 15 min. Compare against your normal level; a sharp drop usually means a carrier/route problem.

panels.title: Long calls now
panels.description: Calls older than each threshold (-long-call-thresholds). Many very long calls with no audio usually means stuck/zombie channels.

panels.title: Unreachable SIP peers
panels.description: chan_sip peers in UNREACHABLE or LAGGED state. 0 is healthy. See the Trunks section for which ones.

panels.title: Unavailable PJSIP contacts
panels.description: PJSIP contacts not answering qualify (OPTIONS). 0 is healthy.

panels.title: Empty bridges
panels.description: Bridges with 0 channels. A few briefly is normal; a number that only grows means an ARI app is not destroying bridges (memory leak).

panels.title: Stasis (ARI) channels
panels.description: Channels currently controlled by an ARI application.

panels.title: Task backlog now
panels.description: Highest queue length across Asterisk taskprocessor types. Should be ~0; sustained values mean Asterisk is overloaded.

panels.title: Exporter dropped events (1h)
panels.description: AMI events the exporter had to drop because it could not keep up. Must be 0; otherwise counters undercount.

panels.title: SIP regs down
panels.description: Outbound chan_sip registrations that are NOT 'Registered' right now (total minus registered). 0 = all trunks registered. Only meaningful on boxes that register out.

panels.title: Availability history
panels.description: Green = up, red = down, per server. Use it to see when Asterisk, AMI or ARI went away and for how long.

panels.title: Calls and channels
panels.description: Channels = call legs (load). Calls = conversations. 'Asterisk active calls' = Asterisk's own dialplan-only count.

panels.title: Call attempts and answers per minute
panels.description: New calls and answered calls per minute (5 min average). The gap between the two lines is unanswered calls.

panels.title: ASR %
panels.description: Answered ÷ attempted, 15 min window. Watch for drops against your usual level.

panels.title: Channels by state
panels.description: Up = talking, Ring/Ringing = waiting for answer, Down = not yet connected (or stuck). A growing Down/Ring share with flat Up = calls are not connecting.

panels.title: Channels by dialplan context
panels.description: Where the traffic is in the dialplan (route / customer view).

panels.title: Long-running calls
panels.description: Calls older than each threshold. Lines that never come down = stuck channels holding capacity.

panels.title: Hangups per minute by cause
panels.description: Why calls end (Q.850 cause codes, 5 min average). 16 = normal. Spikes in 1/3/28 (bad numbers), 17/19/21 (busy/no answer/rejected) or 34/38/41/42 (network/congestion) point to routing or carrier problems.

panels.title: Hangup causes — selected time range
panels.description: Share of each hangup cause over the time range picked at the top.

panels.title: chan_sip peers — status now
panels.description: One row per peer. RTT (ms) from qualify; colour: green < 150 ms, yellow < 300 ms, red above. Negative codes show as text (UNREACHABLE etc.). Use -trunkfile to hide extensions you don't care about.

panels.title: chan_sip peer RTT
panels.description: Qualify round-trip time per reachable peer. Rising RTT usually precedes call-quality complaints.

panels.title: PJSIP contacts — status now
panels.description: One row per PJSIP contact. RTT (ms) from qualify; -1 means not reachable / not qualified.

panels.title: PJSIP contact RTT
panels.description: Qualify round-trip time per available contact.

panels.title: chan_sip channels by trunk
panels.description: Active chan_sip channels per trunk (all states).

panels.title: PJSIP channels by endpoint
panels.description: Active channels per PJSIP endpoint.

panels.title: chan_sip outbound registrations — now
panels.description: One row per outbound registration from 'sip show registry'. State shows the raw Asterisk state (Registered / Request Sent / Rejected / ...). Value 1 = Registered, 0 = anything else. Empty on boxes that do not register out.

panels.title: Outbound registrations: total vs registered
panels.description: How many outbound trunks are configured vs. how many are currently Registered. A gap between the two = a provider registration is down.

panels.title: Outbound dials by trunk — now
panels.description: Channels currently dialling out through each trunk (one per dialling channel; the answering legs are not counted). Same number as counting Dial lines for that trunk in core show channels. Calls placed by Queue, Originate or ARI without Dial are not included.

panels.title: Outbound dials by trunk
panels.description: How many channels were dialling out through each trunk over time. A trunk dropping to zero while others keep dialling usually means that route is down or removed from the dialplan.

options.content:
**How to read QoS.** Values are averaged over calls that are currently up and have enough audio (very short or one-way legs are skipped, see *QoS sample size*).
Rough guide: **packet loss** < 1 % good, > 3 % audible · **jitter** < 30 ms good · **RTT** < 150 ms good. chan_sip is grouped by peer **IP**, PJSIP by **endpoint**.
A one-way leg (e.g. recording) reports no value for the silent direction instead of a fake 100 % loss.

panels.title: PJSIP packet loss %
panels.description: Lost ÷ (received + lost) per endpoint, receive and transmit direction.

panels.title: PJSIP jitter
panels.description: Average jitter per endpoint (ms).

panels.title: PJSIP media RTT
panels.description: Round-trip time measured on live calls (RTCP), per endpoint. Endpoints that do not send RTCP have no line.

panels.title: chan_sip packet loss %
panels.description: Lost ÷ (received + lost) per remote peer IP.

panels.title: chan_sip jitter
panels.description: Average jitter per remote peer IP (ms).

panels.title: QoS sample size
panels.description: How many calls the QoS numbers are based on (measured) vs. skipped as too short / no audio. A QoS value from 1–2 calls is weak evidence.

panels.title: Channels in Stasis (ARI apps)
panels.description: Channels currently handed to ARI applications.

panels.title: Registered ARI apps
panels.description: Number of ARI applications connected to Asterisk. A drop (or 0) means apps disconnected and their calls will fail. Per-group lines appear only if -ari-app-group-regex is set.

panels.title: Bridges: total vs empty
panels.description: Bridges by type and how many have no channels. Empty stasis bridges that only grow = ARI app not destroying bridges (leak).

panels.title: Oldest empty bridge age
panels.description: How long the oldest empty bridge has existed (from ARI). If this keeps climbing for days, bridges are leaking; it resets only when Asterisk restarts or the bridge is destroyed.

panels.title: Taskprocessor queue now
panels.description: Tasks waiting inside Asterisk, by subsystem. Normally ~0. Sustained growth = Asterisk cannot keep up (CPU, slow ARI app, slow DB). Dashed line = Asterisk's default high-water mark (500).

panels.title: Taskprocessor peak depth
panels.description: Highest queue length seen since Asterisk started, by subsystem. A step up means a backlog happened at that time.

panels.title: Asterisk calls processed / min
panels.description: Asterisk's own processed-calls counter, as a rate.

panels.title: Textfile files skipped
panels.description: Custom metric files (textfile collector) that could not be used on the last scrape — the exporter log says why. N/A means the textfile collector is not enabled.

panels.title: Oldest textfile age
panels.description: Time since the least recently updated custom metric file was written. If this keeps growing, the script that writes it has stopped.

panels.title: AMI events per second
panels.description: Events the exporter received (processed) and dropped. Dropped must stay at 0.

panels.title: Collection errors per minute
panels.description: Failed AMI polls and failed ARI polls. Occasional blips are fine; a steady rate means a permission or connectivity problem.
